full_judgment:
2. The case of the plaintiffs in brief was that it was a registered firm and had been carrying on whole-sale and retail business of cotton goods, woolen goods, silk goods, and hosiery goods etc. in the town of Chittagong at its own premises situated at Lakshmi Shaha Road which was formerly known as K.C. Dey Road, Chittagong, being Municipal Holding No. 143/143A of Ander Killa Mohalla which has subsequently been re-numbered as 148. 

 18. Plaintiff has made claim of interest and incidental cost at 10 per cent of the purchase price. And it has also claimed profit at 15 per cent. No evidential was adduced by the plaintiff to how the incidental cost incurred by it for bringing the goods after its purchase to its shop house. There is no evidence before us also to show that the plaintiff would have made profit at 15 per cent if it was free to sell the goods. But undoubtedly the plaintiff incurred some expenses to bring the goods after its purchase to the shop house, and, certainly the plaintiff also would have made some profit by selling the goods. We have allowed interest and incidental cost at 10 per cent of the sale proceeds of the 1st requisitioned goods. As the 1st requisition goods were sold at market price profits must have been included in the priced and as the sale proceeds of the 1st requisitioned goods were lying in the hand of the defendant since 1945 and the plaintiff was deprived of the use of the money so long, so we allowed the plaintiff some interest on that amount. But in case of the 2nd requisition good the compensation was not so long determined so instead of allowing interest on the amount of compensation for 2nd requisitioned goods while determining the compensation we allow the plaintiff an amount at 10 percent of its purchase price towards Incidental cost and loss of profit. While stating prices of the goods which were at C. room the plaintiff included a sum of Rs. 1438 annas profit in the price of the goods. This amount is required to be deducted from the total price stated by the plaintiff in the plaint relating to the goods C-room. The price of the goods at C-room has been stated as Rs. 42,412/5/5. Deducting the sum of Rs. 143/8- annas from this amount of Rs. 42, 4.12/5/3, the purchase price of the goods in C-room stands at Rs. 42,268/13/3. So, the purchase price of all the goods of the 2nd requisition comes to Rs. 1, 64,281/2/9. 10 per cent of this amount comes to Rs. 6,428-1-3 pies, As such, the plaintiff is entitled to recover a sum of Rs. 1, 80, 709/4/as compensation towards the 2nd requisition goods. Hence the plaintiff is entitled in all to a sum of Rs. 2, 78,875-13-6 in respect of the goods of both first and second requisitions.
